chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd al-Razi, from his father, from Salih ibn Uqba, from his father, who said:

I gifted a mule to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so it dislodged the rider which I had sent along with it. So we went over to him (peace be upon him) and we entered Al-Medina. So we informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Why don't you make it sniff the violet (oil)?' So I made it to sniff violet (oil) and it was cured. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Uqba! The violet (oil) is cold in the summer and hot in the winter, soft upon our Shias, dry upon our enemies. Had the people known what was in the violet (oil), they would have evaluated one Owqiya (a unit of measurement) of it, for one Dinar'.
ai.seo_question: What are the medicinal properties and value of violet oil according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical knowledge of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), illustrating the Shia concept of *al-Imam al-Shafi* (the Imam as the healer) who possesses both spiritual and physical remedies. The description of violet oil as 'cooling in summer and warming in winter' reflects the humoral medicine (*Tibb al-Nabawi*) tradition, emphasizing the Imam's role in guiding the community's health and well-being. The concluding remark on its value underscores the hidden wisdom (*Hikmah*) in creation, which is fully realized only through the Imam's insight.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Zayd Al Razy, from his father, from Salih Bin Uqba, from his father who said,

‘I gifted a mule to Abu Abdullahasws, so it dislodged the rider which I had sent along with it.  So we went over to himasws and we entered Al-Medina. So we informed Abu Abdullahasws and heasws said: ‘Why don’t you make it sniff the violet (oil)?’ So I made it to sniff violet (oil) and it was cured. Then heasws said: ‘O Uqba! The violet (oil) is cold in the summer and hot in the winter, soft upon ourasws Shias, dry upon ourasws enemies. Had the people known what was in the violet (oil), they would have evaluated one Owqiya (a unit of measurement) of it, for one Dinar’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn abu Zayd al-Raziy from his father from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from his father who has said the following:

“I once sent a mule as a gift to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, but (on the way) it made the driver to fall off. I then decided to visit him (the Imam) and when we were in al-Madinah, we informed abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must make him (the driver) to sniff viola. He sniffed viola and recovered. He (the Imam) said, ‘O ‘Uqbah, viola is of cool condition in summer and warm in winter. It is soft to our followers and dry to our enemies. If people had known what is in viola, every Awqiyah (a certain measurement) would cost one dinar.’”
